'''''Nerine bowdenii''''' is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] Amaryllidaceae. It is an [[herbaceous plant|herbaceous]] [[bulb]]ous [[perennial plant|perennial]], growing to {{convert|45|cm|0|abbr=on}} tall by {{convert|8|cm|0|abbr=on}}, with strap-shaped leaves and large umbels of lily-like pink flowers in late summer and autumn.<ref name=RHSAZ>{{cite book|title=RHS A-Z encyclopedia of garden plants|year=2008|publisher=Dorling Kindersley|location=United Kingdom|isbn=978-1405332965|pages=1136}}</ref> The [[common names]] of the species are '''Cornish lily''', '''Cape flower''', '''Guernsey lily''', and '''Bowden lily'''. However, it is neither a true [[lilium|lily]] nor from Cornwall or Guernsey, but [[native plant|originates]] from South Africa ([[Eastern Cape]], [[KwaZulu Natal]], [[Free State (province)|Free State]], [[Drakensberg]] Mountains).<ref name=RHSAZ /> Confusingly the name "Guernsey lily" is also applied to a related species, ''[[Nerine sarniensis]]''.

The species was named in 1904 after [[Athelstan Cornish-Bowden]] who had sent bulbs of the plant to England from South Africa.<ref>{{cite journal|first=W.|last= Watson|title=Nerine bowdenii|journal=The Gardeners' Chronicle|volume  =36 third series|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=oE8CAAAAYAAJ&pg=PA365|page=365|date=26 November 1904}}</ref><ref>{{citation|first=John|last=David|title=The Nerine bowdenii story|work=Report of the Proceedings of Hardy Nerine Study Day|date=26 October 2007|url=http://www.nerineandamaryllidsociety.co.uk/media/f7daef5e79c7bb98ffff8013ffffffd3.pdf#page=31|publisher=RHS Herbaceous Plant Committee and the Nerine & Amaryllid Society}}</ref><ref name=TELEG />

==Description==
''N. bowdenii'' bulbs are {{convert|12|to|14|cm}} in circumference.<ref name="Technical">{{cite web |url=http://www.ces.ncsu.edu/depts/hort/consumer/factsheets/bulbs-perennial/Nerinbo.htm |title=Nerine bowdenii |access-date=2010-02-08 |publisher=Holland Technical Service Bulletin |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091125132739/http://www.ces.ncsu.edu/depts/hort/consumer/factsheets/bulbs-perennial/Nerinbo.htm |archive-date=2009-11-25 |url-status=dead }}</ref> The bulbs are "shaped like old-fashioned [[Chianti|Chianti bottles]]".<ref name=TELEG>{{cite news | last=Rees | first=Alun | title=How to grow: Nerine bowdenii | website=Telegraph.co.uk | date=12 November 2013 | url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/gardening/howtogrow/3344719/How-to-grow-Nerine-bowdenii.html | access-date=24 September 2016}}</ref> The plant has eight or more faintly-scented bright pink flowers with frilly tips, resembling finely-cut lilies.<ref>{{cite book | last = Will | first = Giles | title = Encyclopedia of exotic plants for temperate climates | publisher = Timber Press | year = 2007 | pages = 134 | url = https://books.google.com/books?id=Bep5O7D0U34C&q=Nerine+bowdenii&pg=PA135 | isbn = 978-0-88192-785-6 }}</ref> Because the leaves do not appear until spring, the species can tolerate lower temperatures than most species in the [[genus]] ''[[Nerine]]''.<ref>{{cite book | last = Burke | first = Don | title = The complete Burke's backyard: the ultimate book of fact sheets | publisher = Murdoch Books | year = 2005 | pages = 231 | url = https://books.google.com/books?id=MMMjW6AuzHAC&q=Nerine+bowdenii&pg=RA2-PA231 | isbn = 978-1-74045-739-2 }}</ref>

==Cultivation==
''Nerine bowdenii'' is widely cultivated in [[temperateness|temperate]] regions, where it requires warmth and shelter in colder areas, but is quite [[Hardiness (plants)|hardy]], being able to withstand temperatures of {{convert|-15|C|F|abbr=on}}.<ref name=TELEG /> It needs to be planted where it cannot be disturbed for several years, and blooms best when the bulbs are crowded. The species grows best in heat and well-drained soil.<ref>{{cite book | last = Easton | first = Valorie |author2=Hartlage, Richard | title = Plant Life: Growing a Garden in the Pacific Northwest | publisher = Sasquatch Books | year = 2002 | pages = 199 | url = https://books.google.com/books?id=lva7GoINTncC&q=Nerine+bowdenii&pg=PA199 | isbn = 978-1-57061-305-0 }}</ref> However, it will not tolerate [[tropics|tropical]] or very humid weather.<ref>{{cite book | last = Urquhart | first = Paul | title = Growing Bulbs | publisher = Murdoch Books | year = 2004 | pages = 225 | url = https://books.google.com/books?id=6mEl-QbOan4C&q=Nerine+bowdenii&pg=PA225 | isbn = 978-1-74045-520-6 }}</ref><ref>{{cite book | last = Raven | first = Sarah | title = The bold and brilliant garden | publisher = frances lincoln ltd | year = 2001 | pages = 151 | url = https://books.google.com/books?id=alLp_vhefWIC&q=Nerine+bowdenii&pg=PA151 | isbn = 978-0-7112-1752-2 }}</ref> It is suggested that [[colchicum]]s and [[cyclamens]] are good choices of companion plants to grow with this species.<ref name=TELEG />

==Biochemistry==
The bulbs of ''Nerine bowdenii'' contain [[ungeremine]], a [[betaine]]-type [[alkaloid]], and a number of other [[alkaloid]]s.<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1021/ja01495a057|last=Lyle|first=R. E.|author2=E. A. Kielar |author3=J. R. Crowder |author4=W. C. Wildman |year=1960|title=The Alkaloids of Nerine bowdenii W. Wats. and Crinum moorei J. D. Hook.|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society |volume=82 |issue=10|pages=2620–2625|bibcode=1960JAChS..82.2620L }}</ref> Ungeremine is an [[acetylcholinesterase inhibitor|inhibitor of acetylcholinesterase]], and as such may be of interest in research into treatment of [[Alzheimer's disease]]. Ungeremine also has been isolated from a number of related plant species, such as ''[[Ungernia minor]]'', ''[[Ungernia spiralis]]'', ''[[Zephyranthes flava]]'', ''[[Crinum asiaticum]]'', ''[[Crinum augustum]]'', ''[[Pancratium maritimum]]'' and ''[[Hippeastrum solandriflorum]]''.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Rhee IK|first=I|author2=Appels N|author3=Hofte B|author4=Karabatak B|author5=Erkelens C|author6=Stark LM|author7=Flippin LA|author8=Verpoorte R|date=November 2004|title=Isolation of the Acetylcholinesterase Inhibitor Ungeremine from Nerine bowdenii by Preparative HPLC Coupled On-Line to a Flow Assay System|journal=Biological & Pharmaceutical Bulletin|volume=27|issue=11|pages=1804–1809|pmid=15516727|doi=10.1248/bpb.27.1804|doi-access=free}}</ref>

==Diseases==
The [[plant virus]], [[vallota mosaic virus]], has been found to infect ''Nerine bowdenii'' and other members of the genus ''Nerine'' in the UK.<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1111/j.1365-3059.2008.01850.x|last=Monger|first=W. A. |author2=R. A. Mumford|date=18 July 2008|title=Vallota mosaic virus infecting nerine in the UK|journal=Plant Pathology |volume=57|issue=4|pages=768|doi-access=free}}</ref>
